questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: Under RBI's Master Direction on KYC, which of the following is NOT listed as an 'Officially Valid Document' (OVD) for proof of identity and address?

options.text: Voter's Identity Card issued by the Election Commission of India
Job card issued by NREGA duly signed by an officer of the State Government

solution.explanation: The KYC Direction lists the passport, the driving licence, proof of possession of Aadhaar, the Voter's Identity Card, the NREGA job card signed by a State Government officer and the letter of the National Population Register as OVDs. The PAN is collected separately (or Form 60) but is not an OVD for address.
steps: OVD list: passport, driving licence, Aadhaar possession proof, Voter ID, NREGA job card, NPR letter
PAN card is not on the list
solution.why_others_wrong: Passport, Voter ID and the signed NREGA job card are all named OVDs.
solution.final_answer: Option A: PAN card

fact_checks.claim: OVD means the passport, the driving licence, proof of possession of Aadhaar number, the Voter's Identity Card issued by the Election Commission of India, job card issued by NREGA duly signed by an officer of the State Government and letter issued by the National Population Register

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: Under RBI's KYC Direction, how often must periodic updation of KYC be carried out for high-risk, medium-risk and low-risk customers respectively?

options.text: Every year, every 5 years and every 10 years
At least once in 2 years, 5 years and 8 years
At least once in 3 years, 8 years and 12 years
At least once in 2 years, 8 years and 10 years

solution.explanation: Regulated entities follow a risk-based approach: KYC is updated at least once every two years for high-risk customers, once every eight years for medium-risk customers and once every ten years for low-risk customers.
solution.why_others_wrong: The other combinations do not match the 2/8/10-year schedule in the Direction.
solution.final_answer: Option D: At least once in 2 years, 8 years and 10 years

fact_checks.claim: Periodic updation at least once in every two years for high-risk customers, once in every eight years for medium risk customers and once in every ten years for low-risk customers

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: How does RBI's KYC Direction treat Video-based Customer Identification Process (V-CIP)?

options.text: As permissible only for customers who already hold another account with the same bank
As a method usable only for opening small accounts with limited credits
As an alternate method of identification with facial recognition through live audio-visual interaction, treated on par with face-to-face identification
As valid only when the customer is physically present at a branch

solution.explanation: V-CIP is defined as an alternate method of customer identification with facial recognition and customer due diligence by an authorised official through seamless, secure, live, informed-consent based audio-visual interaction, and it is treated as on par with face-to-face identification.
steps: V-CIP = live audio-visual interaction + facial recognition
solution.why_others_wrong: V-CIP is not restricted to existing customers or to small accounts, and it does not require branch presence.
solution.final_answer: Option C: As an alternate method of identification with facial recognition through live audio-visual interaction, treated on par with face-to-face identification

fact_checks.claim: V-CIP: an alternate method of customer identification with facial recognition and customer due diligence by an authorised official through live audio-visual interaction; treated on par with face-to-face CIP

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: Under RBI's KYC framework, what is the 'KYC Identifier'?

options.text: The account number of the customer's first bank account
The unique number or code assigned to a customer by the Central KYC Records Registry
The Legal Entity Identifier of the bank that did the KYC

solution.explanation: The Central KYC Records Registry (CKYCR) receives, stores, safeguards and retrieves KYC records in digital form. The KYC Identifier is the unique number or code it assigns to a customer, which other regulated entities can use to fetch the KYC records.
steps: KYC Identifier = unique code assigned by CKYCR
solution.why_others_wrong: It is not an account number, the Aadhaar number or an LEI.
solution.final_answer: Option C: The unique number or code assigned to a customer by the Central KYC Records Registry

fact_checks.claim: KYC Identifier means the unique number or code assigned to a customer by the Central KYC Records Registry; CKYCR receives, stores, safeguards and retrieves KYC records in digital form

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: According to RBI, which of the following is NOT a difference between a bank and a Non-Banking Financial Company (NBFC)?

options.text: NBFCs do not form part of the payment and settlement system and cannot issue cheques drawn on themselves
Deposit insurance from DICGC is not available to depositors of NBFCs

solution.explanation: RBI lists three differences: an NBFC cannot accept demand deposits; it is not part of the payment and settlement system and cannot issue cheques drawn on itself; and its depositors do not get DICGC deposit insurance. NBFCs do lend to individuals.
steps: Differences: no demand deposits; no cheques/payment system; no DICGC cover
Lending to individuals is permitted → not a difference
solution.why_others_wrong: The other three are exactly the differences RBI lists.
solution.final_answer: Option D: NBFCs cannot lend to individuals

fact_checks.claim: NBFCs cannot accept demand deposits; do not form part of the payment and settlement system and cannot issue cheques drawn on itself; deposit insurance facility of DICGC is not available to depositors of NBFCs

In Special Economic Zones, functioning as virtual foreign branches located in India
In every district headquarters, as rural branches
In GIFT City only, as branches of foreign central banks

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: The Cheque Truncation System (CTS) was introduced in grids. In which order were the three grids set up?

solution.explanation: RBI's payments booklet records that CTS was introduced in New Delhi after a pilot in 2008, extended to Chennai in September 2011 and to Mumbai in April 2013. All MICR centres were later subsumed into grid-based CTS.
solution.why_others_wrong: Only the first option has both the correct order and the correct years.
solution.final_answer: Option A: New Delhi (2008), Chennai (2011), Mumbai (2013)

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: Ravi holds a 'small account' opened under RBI's KYC Direction. In the current financial year the aggregate credits are ₹95,000, his balance has never exceeded ₹40,000, and in October his withdrawals and transfers add up to ₹12,000. Which statement is correct?

options.text: All limits are respected, since the annual credit limit is ₹2 lakh
The balance breaches the ₹25,000 limit for small accounts
The October withdrawals breach the ₹10,000 monthly limit; the credit and balance limits are respected
Only the credits breach the limit, which is ₹50,000 a year

solution.explanation: A small account allows aggregate credits of up to ₹1 lakh in a financial year, aggregate withdrawals and transfers of up to ₹10,000 in a month, and a balance of up to ₹50,000 at any time. Credits of ₹95,000 and a balance of ₹40,000 are within limits; withdrawals of ₹12,000 in a month exceed ₹10,000.
solution.why_others_wrong: The annual credit limit is ₹1 lakh (not ₹2 lakh or ₹50,000), and the balance limit is ₹50,000 (not ₹25,000).
solution.final_answer: Option C: The October withdrawals breach the ₹10,000 monthly limit; the credit and balance limits are respected

fact_checks.claim: Small account: aggregate of all credits in a financial year does not exceed rupees one lakh; aggregate of all withdrawals and transfers in a month does not exceed rupees ten thousand; balance at any point of time does not exceed rupees fifty thousand

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text:
A customer opened a deposit account and a term-loan account with a bank through Aadhaar OTP-based e-KYC in non-face-to-face mode. Under RBI's KYC Direction, which of the following is permitted?
P. Keeping an aggregate balance of ₹1.2 lakh in the deposit account
Q. Aggregate credits of ₹1.8 lakh in the deposit account in the financial year
R. A term loan of ₹50,000 sanctioned in the year

solution.concept: Limits on accounts opened by OTP-based e-KYC
solution.explanation: For accounts opened with OTP-based e-KYC in non-face-to-face mode, the aggregate deposit balance cannot exceed ₹1 lakh, aggregate credits in a financial year cannot exceed ₹2 lakh, and term loans sanctioned cannot exceed ₹60,000 in a year. P breaches the balance cap; Q and R are within limits.
solution.why_others_wrong: Any option containing P is wrong; 'R only' wrongly excludes Q.
solution.final_answer: Option A: Q and R only

fact_checks.claim: OTP-based e-KYC accounts: aggregate balance of all deposit accounts shall not exceed rupees one lakh; aggregate of all credits in a financial year shall not exceed rupees two lakh; aggregate amount of term loans sanctioned shall not exceed rupees sixty thousand in a year

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: Meena pays an annual locker rent of ₹4,500. A fire at the branch, caused by the bank's negligence, destroys locker contents worth ₹6 lakh. Applying RBI's revised locker instructions of 18 August 2021 (in force from 1 January 2022), what is the most the bank is liable to pay?

options.text: Nothing, because lockers are at the hirer's risk

solution.explanation: Under the August 2021 instructions, for loss of locker contents due to fire, theft, burglary, building collapse or fraud by employees, the bank's liability is limited to 100 times the prevailing annual rent. 100 × ₹4,500 = ₹4.5 lakh, which is less than the ₹6 lakh lost.
solution.why_others_wrong: The bank does not pay the full value beyond the cap; ₹45,000 uses 10 times the rent; banks are liable for fire losses caused by their negligence.
solution.final_answer: Option B: ₹4.5 lakh

fact_checks.claim: RBI circular of 18 August 2021 (in force from 1 January 2022): liability for loss of locker contents due to fire, theft, burglary, dacoity, robbery, building collapse or employee fraud is one hundred times the prevailing annual rent

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: At the time of allotting a locker with annual rent of ₹3,200, a bank asks the new hirer for a term deposit as security. If the charges for breaking open the locker are ₹2,400, what is the largest term deposit the bank can ask for under RBI's revised locker instructions of 18 August 2021?

solution.explanation: Banks may obtain a term deposit at the time of allotment that covers three years' rent and the charges for breaking open the locker in case of need: 3 × 3,200 + 2,400 = ₹12,000.
solution.why_others_wrong: ₹9,600 omits break-open charges; ₹5,600 is one year's rent plus charges; ₹3.2 lakh is the 100-times liability cap, not the deposit.
solution.final_answer: Option D: ₹12,000

fact_checks.claim: RBI circular of 18 August 2021: banks may obtain a Term Deposit at the time of allotment covering three years' rent and the charges for breaking open the locker

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: On 27 January 1921, three Presidency banks were merged to form which bank?

solution.explanation: SBI traces its origin to the Bank of Calcutta (1806). On 27 January 1921 the three Presidency banks (Bengal, Bombay and Madras) were merged to form the Imperial Bank of India, which became SBI in 1955.
steps: Bank of Bengal + Bank of Bombay + Bank of Madras → Imperial Bank of India (1921)
solution.why_others_wrong: SBI was created from the Imperial Bank only in 1955; PNB and Bank of India were separate banks.
solution.final_answer: Option D: Imperial Bank of India

fact_checks.claim: On 27 January 1921, the three banks were merged to form the Imperial Bank of India

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: In May 2011 RBI moved to a single independently varying policy rate (the repo rate), with the reverse repo pegged below it and a new MSF above it. This followed the recommendations of the Working Group on Operating Procedure of Monetary Policy chaired by:

solution.concept: Committees and the operating procedure of monetary policy
solution.explanation: RBI's Bulletin notes that the new operating procedure, operational from May 2011, followed the Working Group on Operating Procedures of Monetary Policy chaired by Deepak Mohanty: the repo became the only independently varying policy rate, the reverse repo was pegged 100 bps below it and the MSF was set 100 bps above it.
steps: Mohanty Working Group → single policy rate (repo), May 2011
solution.why_others_wrong: Urjit Patel chaired the 2014 committee on the monetary policy framework; Rajan chaired the 2008 committee on financial sector reforms; Jalan chaired the committee on RBI's economic capital framework.
solution.final_answer: Option A: Deepak Mohanty

fact_checks.claim: Following the recommendations of the Working Group on Operating Procedures of Monetary Policy (Chairman: Shri Deepak Mohanty), the repo rate has become the only independently varying policy rate; operational from May 2011

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text:
Consider the following statements about the origins of the State Bank of India:
I. SBI's origin goes back to the Bank of Calcutta, established in June 1806, which became the Bank of Bengal on receiving its charter.
II. The Imperial Bank of India was formed in 1921 by merging three Presidency banks.
III. The Bank of Bombay was the oldest of the three Presidency banks.
Which of the above is/are correct?

solution.explanation: SBI's history begins with the Bank of Calcutta (2 June 1806), redesignated the Bank of Bengal when it received its charter. The Imperial Bank of India was formed on 27 January 1921 by merging the three Presidency banks. The Bank of Bombay (1840) was younger than the Bank of Calcutta/Bengal, so III is wrong.
steps: III: wrong (Bank of Calcutta/Bengal, 1806, was the oldest)
solution.why_others_wrong: III is false, which eliminates the options containing it; 'II only' omits the correct statement I.
solution.final_answer: Option C: I and II only

fact_checks.claim: Origin of SBI goes back to the establishment of the Bank of Calcutta in Calcutta on 2 June 1806; three years later it received its charter and was redesigned as the Bank of Bengal; on 27 January 1921 the three banks were merged to form the Imperial Bank of India

solution.why_others_wrong: Deshmukh was the third Governor, Rama Rau the fourth and Iengar the sixth.
solution.final_answer: Option B: Sir James Taylor

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: Which of the following is a wholly owned subsidiary of the Reserve Bank of India?

options.text: Indian Financial Technology and Allied Services (IFTAS)
Small Industries Development Bank of India (SIDBI)

solution.explanation: RBI's fully owned subsidiaries are DICGC, BRBNMPL, ReBIT, IFTAS and the Reserve Bank Innovation Hub (RBIH). NPCI is owned by banks; CCIL and SIDBI are not RBI subsidiaries.
steps: Subsidiaries: DICGC, BRBNMPL, ReBIT, IFTAS, RBIH
solution.why_others_wrong: NPCI is a bank-promoted not-for-profit company; CCIL is promoted by banks and institutions; SIDBI is a separate development financial institution.
solution.final_answer: Option A: Indian Financial Technology and Allied Services (IFTAS)

fact_checks.claim: Fully owned subsidiaries: DICGC, BRBNMPL, ReBIT, Indian Financial Technology and Allied Services (IFTAS), Reserve Bank Innovation Hub (RBIH)

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: RBI lists five training establishments. Which one of them is an autonomous institute rather than part of RBI?

options.text: Reserve Bank of India Staff College (RBSC)
Institute for Development and Research in Banking Technology (IDRBT)

solution.explanation: RBI has five training establishments. Four are part of RBI — RBSC, CAB, the Enterprise Computing and Cybersecurity Training Institute (ECCTI) and the College of Supervisors — while IDRBT is autonomous.
steps: Part of RBI: RBSC, CAB, ECCTI, CoS

solution.final_answer: Option C: Institute for Development and Research in Banking Technology (IDRBT)

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: RBI's list of Governors shows A. Ghosh serving from 15 January 1985 to 4 February 1985, when R. N. Malhotra took over. For how many days did Ghosh hold office (counting from his first day up to, but not including, 4 February)?

solution.explanation: From 15 January to 4 February 1985 there are 16 days left in January after the 15th plus 4 days in February, i.e. 20 days — the shortest tenure in RBI's list.
solution.why_others_wrong: 31, 45 and 14 days do not match the dates.
solution.final_answer: Option A: 20 days

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: Sir Benegal Rama Rau was Governor from 1 July 1949 to 14 January 1957, and Shaktikanta Das from 12 December 2018 to 10 December 2024. Which statement is correct?

options.text: Das served longer, by about one year
Both served almost exactly six years
Rama Rau served about 7.5 years, roughly 1.5 years longer than Das's 6 years
Rama Rau served about 5.5 years, half a year less than Das

solution.explanation: 1 July 1949 to 14 January 1957 is about 7 years 6½ months (≈7.5 years). 12 December 2018 to 10 December 2024 is just under 6 years. Rama Rau's tenure, the longest in RBI's list, exceeds Das's by about 1.5 years.
solution.why_others_wrong: The other options misstate one or both tenures.
solution.final_answer: Option C: Rama Rau served about 7.5 years, roughly 1.5 years longer than Das's 6 years

fact_checks.claim: Sir Benegal Rama Rau 01-07-1949 to 14-01-1957; Shri Shaktikanta Das 12-12-2018 to 10-12-2024

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: According to RBI's status release of 1 January 2026, what share of the ₹2000 banknotes in circulation on 19 May 2023 (when their withdrawal was announced) had been returned by 31 December 2025?

options.text: 100%; the notes are no longer legal tender

solution.explanation: ₹2000 notes worth ₹3.56 lakh crore were in circulation on 19 May 2023; by the close of 31 December 2025 only ₹5,669 crore remained, so 98.41% had been returned. The notes continue to be legal tender.

questions.question_text: In March 2026, RBI fixed the Ways and Means Advances (WMA) limit for the Government of India for April–September 2026 at:

solution.explanation: RBI's press release of 27 March 2026 set the WMA limit for H1 2026-27 at ₹2,50,000 crore, fixed in consultation with the Government. RBI may trigger fresh market borrowing when 75% of the limit is used.
solution.why_others_wrong: ₹1,50,000 crore was the limit for the first half of earlier years; the others do not match.

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: According to RBI, what minimum Net Owned Fund (NOF) is now required for registration as an NBFC, and by when must existing NBFCs reach it?

options.text: ₹25 lakh; no deadline for existing NBFCs

solution.explanation: RBI's NBFC FAQs state that a company needs a minimum NOF of ₹10 crore to register as an NBFC; new applicants must have it from the start and existing NBFCs must reach it by 31 March 2027.
